messages.text: Mama Denise, can you call when you get off? Hattie ran through the last few diapers faster than I thought.
Morning baby. I can bring a small pack by after cafeteria duty and I will keep her name lifted at noon.
Thank you. I did not want to make a whole thing of it, just needed to check with you first.
That is fine. Text Keisha too if you need wipes before I get there.
I saw that clip everybody keeps sending. I am not passing it to Mama tonight because she will be up fussing.
Tiana said keep it off the main feed and we can talk once Hattie is asleep.
Good. Same talk as always: stay calm, keep your hands where they can see, ask for the badge number, and call home.
Denise wants everybody on the house phone after church Sunday, not arguing in comments.
Left the ripe avocado half in the little blue bowl. She made that face at the oatmeal again.
Try the avocado first, then the orange mash. Tiny spoon, no chunks.
Avocado got claps. Orange bowl got two big smiles. She slapped the tray after the banana cup was gone too.
That tray slap usually means she wants another spoonful.
How did the little boss do at her appointment?
She fussed for the shots then wanted my keys. They said keep doing the soft foods and let her practice tiny lumpy bites.
That sounds like her. Did they say anything about the ear pulling?
Just watch it if a fever comes with it. No extra visit unless that changes.
She woke up pointing at the remote when the cowboy was on the screen.
Keep it short and sit with her. She was already squealing at that little dinosaur earlier.
I gave her six minutes before bath. The spaceman fell over and she did that belly laugh.
Good. Then no more screen after pajamas.
News had that clip from downtown again. I turned it down before baby girl started clapping at the TV like it was Fenway.
Thank you. Mama called right after and said folks at church are asking about the town hall and the school board seat.
Yeah. Between the grocery bill and them talking about patrols near the apartments, everybody got something to say.
I saved the candidate sheet by the diaper bag so we can look after her bath.
Community center has the stroller circle Thursday at 10. Ms. Angela said they are saving spots for the babies from our side of town.
Thank you. I want Hattie around aunties who already know how to speak up when offices act like the list is suddenly full.
Bring her paperwork and I will sit with you. They move different when somebody from church is standing there too.
That helps. I keep telling myself she has more people around her than the mess waiting outside.
Breakfast went better after I ran the banana and sweet potato through the blender again.
I put the faucet ticket in the portal before breakfast. The office said somebody may stop by this afternoon.
I put on the red fuzzy one while I warmed her breakfast. Soon as the beat started, her little hands started going.
Did she keep any of it down before trying to crawl under the chair?
Tell them to text first. Hattie finally settled after those cars kept roaring down the road.
She did the same yesterday when that counting clip came on. Scooted straight across the mat like she had somewhere to be.
Most of it. She swatted the spoon when I added those tiny green rounds, so I just stopped and let her scoot around a minute.
I will. Mrs. Green next door said she will keep an eye out if a truck pulls up while I am feeding her.
Then looked at the spoon and said more for the banana. I saved the rest for after nap.
I will leave the bowl plain for lunch and keep the floor blanket out.
Good. The morning line from Bragg had Ramsey Street crawling again, so I may be late getting back.
She woke up mad after that delivery truck horn. I took her to the back room and held her a minute.
Did she come around?
Mostly. I had Mama's little church voice note ready too, but she was already slowing down once I had her tucked in.
If she starts up again before nap, I'll play Denise's clip and rock her by the fan.
Mama sent a voice note humming that slow organ song again. Hattie stopped fussing before the first verse was over.
She knows that tune already. She reached for the phone like she knew Grandma was on it.
I saved it for bedtime. Also putting aside soft sweet potatoes from the pan before everybody adds pepper.
Good. That and the quiet singing usually settles her after a busy house.
She crawled straight to Keisha's shiny bracelet, patted it twice, then backed into my knees when the boys started racing through the hall.
I saw that. She was smiling at them until the hallway got loud.
I'm going to keep the front bedroom open Sunday. If the laughing gets big again, I'll take her in there with the piano playlist.
Mama sent a voice note of that old choir song for Hattie's bedtime. I saved it with the other sleepy songs.
Play the soft one first. She settled quick when Denise hummed it after Sunday dinner.
I will. Tomorrow I am putting the little board book with Harriet on top, but only the smiling pages before nap.
Good. Let her hear the names and the songs while the room stays calm.
I sorted the 18 month sleepers and two packs of wipes. Want me to drop them after my shift?
Yes please. We are stretching this week until Marcus's Friday deposit hits.
No problem. I can sit with Hattie for an hour too if Tiana needs to run to Food Lion.
That would help. We are doing rice, beans, and chicken at home tonight anyway.
I got the picture from Saturday. Want me to send it to Grandma and Monique, or keep it just between us?
Send it in the family thread please. Just that one with her dress straight, not the crying one.
Got it. I cropped out the other kids too.
Thank you. I do not want a bunch of folks saving every little moment.
I put the Saturday nursery-room sign-up on the church page. Tiana can just tap her name under the 10:30 slot.
I will remind her. She saw the picture you added of Hattie by the hymnals and smiled at it.
Good. I also sent her the banana-oat idea in the little parents thread, but tell her to ask Dr. Benson if she is unsure about anything new.
I put Hattie's birthday cash and the diaper receipts in the blue folder before work.
Can you set aside those 12 month sleepers? The cuffs are getting tight on her again.
Okay. I will leave that folder alone and keep the Walmart receipt from today in there too.
I put three in the top drawer and left the snug ones in the laundry basket.
Thank you. I am not chasing bows and matching sets when she pulls everything off anyway 😂
Good. Until any county letter has her name and a number on it, I am only planning around our checks and what family brings.
Keisha said she may have a small bag from the twins that could get us through this size.
That makes sense. I will not count anything extra when I write the March list.
I moved the bins off the bottom shelf. She made it from the rug to that cabinet before I could fold one towel.
After breakfast she kept patting the basil by the steps while I filled the little can.
I finished Hattie's community center packet. The boxes about adult paperwork in the home are all marked no.
Good call. She was doing the same thing with the bumpy basket yesterday, straight across the room.
She likes when the water hits the dirt. I had to move her hand before she grabbed a wet handful.
Good. She only needed the shot page and the emergency names, right?
Yes. Her part was birthday, pediatrician, diapers, and nap notes. She tried to chew the pen the whole time.
Leave the chunky toy pieces on the mat, though. She kept taking two apart, turning them, and trying them the other way.
Let her get a few minutes there, then crib by 10:30. That combo worked yesterday.
I will set those out after breakfast and keep the cabinet doors latched.
That sounds like Hattie helping.
Morning, Tiana. I saw that long post going around about delaying the 12-month visit stuff. Did the office give y'all anything in writing yesterday?
Yes ma'am. The nurse printed two pages and Dr. Rana marked the next date on her little card.
Good. I would keep those pages in the diaper bag for daycare and call the office if the post has you wondering.
That's what I'm doing. I put the post away until I can ask through the portal.
Did Hattie make it through the mat room yesterday? I saw Ms. Alisha setting the colored strips out when I passed by.
She did. Soon as the shaker started, she went straight after the two babies in front of her.
That sounds like her. Those short bursts may help before nap now that she is crossing the room so fast.
I can stop by around 11 if Tiana needs to run to the store. Want me to bring the 18-month sleepers too?
Yes please. Morning bottle is done and she is crawling around the living room now.
Good. I will keep it quiet when I come in so she still gets that noon rest.
Thank you. Tiana put the stroller by the door in case you take her around the block.
Pulling in after this last delivery. Need me to grab diapers before I get home?
Yes, size 4. Denise left the last pack by the crib, but we're down to six.
Got it. If your mama comes by for bath time, tell her I saved her the good Red Sox chair.
She said just a quick stop. Hattie already has your cap in her hands.
Good morning, Tiana. They moved the little ones at the center to 10:30 today, after the older kids clear out.
Thank you. I have her water diaper and towel by the door, so 10:30 works better.
Perfect. If the room by the pool gets loud, step into the hallway before you head over to the mats.
That is the plan. She did better last week when we waited until the first bunch of babies got settled.
I found that little blue cover in the suitcase pocket. Same one she had clenched the whole time by the rail.
Keep it out for nap. She settled fast when I tucked it beside her after all that wind.
Yes. And next time I am bringing the clip-on fan for the stroller, because that sun was not playing.
Put it with the travel wipes. The wheels still have sand in them.
Text me a photo of the clinic sheet before you turn it in. They get picky when the first-year boxes and the date line do not match.
I will. Tiana only has the discharge packet and the bracelet in the drawer, no full line written anywhere.
Then leave it blank until the nurse checks their system. Bring her shot card too, just in case.
Got it. She has been fine since Wednesday, just sleepy after the appointment.
Cousins are getting loud over here. Want me to tell them we are leaving right after dinner?
Yes. She already crawled under the side table when everybody clapped at the TV.
Got it. I will grab the bag and keep the car warm.
I have her on my shoulder with the little piano track. She is not ready for more passing around.
First pitch is 7:05. I put her blanket on the couch already.
Good. I will do her bottle first so she is settled before the loud parts.
She was staring hard at the screen last time. When the park got loud she started patting both hands.
Leave the little cap out, but if she rubs her eyes we are switching to music.
Baby girl looked so calm in that window-seat picture you showed me after service.
She watched the trees the whole way, then knocked out as soon as we got to Nana and Papa.
That is good practice for bigger family outings. Keep that little ears jar where folks can drop change after church.
Tiana put it by the kitchen door. Marcus keeps joking she needs her first pair before we go south.
I packed the diaper bag light today: puree pouch, two bibs, wipes, and the one tiny cup.
Good. Marcus said he will carry the folded stroller after service.
That works. I wrote Hattie's name on the nursery sticker so nobody mixes her bag with the cousins' bags.
I'll keep the extra pacifier in the side pocket.
She finished most of the oatmeal after I thinned it out. I am doing floor toys before she rubs her eyes.
Good. I put the soft piano playlist back on the speaker if she starts fighting the crib.
Perfect. I changed her already, so after a little stacking cup time I will try laying her down.
Text me if she wakes quick. I can warm the sweet potatoes before lunch.
Morning baby. I put aside two board books from the cafeteria giveaway and that little shape sorter from church.
Thank you, Mama. She loves the red circle piece, even if most of it still goes straight to her mouth.
That is how they learn. I can come by after my shift and show her the clapping song my grandma used with us.
Come after 4:30 if you can. I want her hearing those old songs from you, not just videos.
Morning baby. How did my girl sleep after all that clapping and those doors yesterday?
She went right for the measuring cups at your house, then buried her face in Tiana's shirt when the cousins came back through.
Bless her heart. I noticed she peeked out when the boys made silly faces, then tucked back in when they got wound up.
Tiana sat with her in the back room and put on that soft piano track. She settled enough to take the pouch before we left.
Baby girl settle down after all that clapping at choir practice?
Yes ma'am. I took her to the back room, dimmed the light, and played that piano playlist. She rubbed her blanket and was babbling again before bath.
Good. I can sit with her Friday if you need to pick up diapers or call the office about that June card.
Thank you. I put the card on the fridge so I don't lose the date this time.
Good morning, baby. Do you still need me to ride with y'all to Little Tumbles after breakfast?
Yes ma'am. I added the 10:30 spot because she was doing laps from the sofa to the kitchen before 8.
I will bring the little leggings. Last time she kept sliding past that blue strip when the other babies took off.
Thank you. I am hoping it wears her out enough for a real nap.
I can come by after my shift. I also found Hattie some soft headbands and the little satin sleep cap at the Raeford shop.
Perfect. Her curls are rubbing out in the back and I do not want to fight dry patches again.
Got you. And about that daycare packet, write down every call and who told you what. Do not let them slide you behind people who applied later.
I saved the voicemails. I am trying to stay hopeful, but I am tired of having to prove we asked on time.
Did Hattie knock out after the place with the foam steps?
Yes, before we got home. She watched those two little boys crawl through the tunnel and wore herself out trying to follow.
That counts as her workout. Need me to rinse the blue suit for Saturday?
Please. The center bag still has wet socks in it too.
I switched from the game during commercials and she forgot all about my hat.
Was it the one with the big red face again?
Yep. She slapped both hands together, laughed, then took off crawling like she was rounding third.
Give her the last banana bites before she gets too wound up.
Your mama had Hattie clapping to those old Al Green and Temptations tracks while I was trying to fold towels.
She likes the hand claps and the low voices. Same face she makes when the choir warms up.
Denise said save her a plate Saturday if Keisha cooks. Mac, beans, the soft yams, all that.
I will. Hattie can have the plain yams before the big folks season everything.
We are setting up the little ones in the back room Sunday, away from the clapping and speakers.
Thank you. If too many new faces walk through, Tiana may step out with Hattie by the side door.
That is fine. Denise and Sister Althea will be right there too, so y'all will have familiar hands.
Good. We are not doing the Bragg family fair afterward; the flyer asked for an ID we do not have anyway.
I watched WRAL while she ate sweet potatoes. They said the clinic bus may lose Saturday hours.
That would make shots and checkups harder for a lot of mamas. Add it to the list for Nana to ask about Sunday.
Already did. Also groceries jumped again, so I am comparing the food help notes Monique sent.
After nap we can read the sample ballot blurbs, especially the ones about school meals and clinic funding.
Baby, I got your voice note. Do not take Hattie anywhere near that courthouse crowd tomorrow.
We are staying in. Marcus said he will watch the video later after dinner.
That is better. I can talk plain in the living room and remind the young ones how to answer, how to stand, and when to be quiet.
I will put the phone on speaker once Hattie is settled.
Hey baby, I left that 38 second voice note in the thread. Play it low if Hattie fights sleep again.
Tiana has her on her shoulder right now. She got quieter as soon as Tiana picked her up.
Good. Let Tiana keep that rhythm. If she pops back up, put my note on and I will call after I finish these dishes.
I found a Target bag in my hall closet: two zip sleepers, four onesies, and little gray pants. Mostly 18 month.
That would help. The 12 month stack is shrinking fast.
I will drop it after my shift. Wash them once and keep whatever fits.
Perfect. She will not care what color the pants are as long as she can crawl.
I saw Tiana's clip of Hattie smacking the spoon on Instagram. She is serious about that avocado.
She laughed after Marcus replayed it twice. Tiana is asking the moms page if anyone freezes tiny portions without them turning brown.
Lemon can be too sharp for her right now, so have Tiana check before copying somebody's trick. I can bring the silicone tray Sunday.
That helps. I will tell her to keep the question for the visit note and use the tray for sweet potatoes first.
I am leaving Raeford in about 20. You still want me to look at that paper from Cape Fear Pediatrics?
Yes please. The nurse said it was routine, but I like hearing it from somebody who knows Hattie too.
Bring it out when I get there. I can also drop the 12-month clothes Aunt Pam set aside.
Perfect. I only asked you and Mama about it, so we can talk before dinner.
Did she take the afternoon bottle or just throw the cup again?
Mostly threw it. She did eat sweet potatoes and then pulled every block out of the basket.
I will grab diapers on the way. If she is up after dinner we can let her clap through the first inning.
That should work if bedtime music starts by 7:30.
She just stared at the waves on my phone like she remembered that long morning.
Did she reach for the blanket again?
Yep, grabbed the corner and sat still. Crowd noise in the clip did not bother her this time.
That was exactly how she looked sitting in the stroller while everybody else walked closer.
For the nursery form, the community center can take a month and year if the family is waiting on the official copy.
That helps. Tiana keeps saying it was the Fayetteville hospital week, but nobody wants to guess the box.
Yes ma'am, let the office fill it in. I can still add Hattie to the little walkers list for late March.
Please do. She likes the soft mats more than the busy room.
The community center has a 9:30 circle time Tuesday, but it fills up fast.
Thank you. I may just bring her for the songs and come back home before lunch.
That sounds right. Denise told me Hattie does best when one of her people keeps the same snack and nap rhythm.
Exactly. Marcus is off that afternoon too, so we can keep it light.
Baby girl looked so sweet at the community center today. Do you want the little walking clip I took?
Community center has the free toddler play hour Tuesday morning. I can save Hattie a spot if y'all can make it.
Yes ma'am, text it to me. Please do not send it around yet; Marcus wants to check it first.
Please do. We skipped the paid gym day this month and need something close by.
I understand. Bring her cup and snack from home, and I will check the donation table for diapers.
Of course. I kept her name tag out of the frame.
I appreciate that. If we use any, it will just be one short clip for close family.
Thank you. Tiana is trying to keep the card clear in case the van acts up again.
Marcus, can you check Hattie's thighs when you change her? The tiny bandages came off but I want to see if the spots look calm.
Looks fine. She's crawling after the blocks like nothing happened.
Good. The after-care sheet said to call if fever gets high or she cries hard for hours.
Keeping the sheet on the fridge. And no random comment-section cures from Auntie group chat tonight, promise.
Hey baby, I can stop by after church kitchen cleanup. Did she get her lunch down yet?
Half the avocado, then a clean diaper and the stroller around the block. She is blinking slow now.
I will come quiet. If she fusses, I can do that low Sunday hum she likes while you get the room dark.
That may help. I am trying to get this second sleep before everybody comes by later.
Baby girl looked worn out after the birthday song. Did she settle once y'all got home?
She cried in the hallway, then reached for Tiana and buried her face.
Put that soft song on low. I can send the hum voice note again if she keeps fighting sleep.
Please send it. We moved her mat to the back bedroom and closed the door halfway.
Baby girl still wearing that red B shirt tonight or did it already get sweet potatoes on it?
It survived lunch. Marcus said she needs it for the game after bath.
Send me a picture when she starts watching the room holler. That hand clap makes me laugh.
I found that picture of your granddaddy in his church suit. Want me to print it before Keisha comes by?
Yes, small copy for Hattie's room. Put it beside the family reunion one, not over the crib.
Got it. I will tell her he sang bass and worked two jobs, not the hard parts.
Exactly. Faces, names, songs, and what they built. She can learn the rest in little pieces.
I can swing by Mazarick after my route if she wakes up decent.
She ate at 2:50 and is down now. If she pops up before 4, we can do one lap.
Cool. I’ll bring the stroller fan. No long visit, just trees and back home before dinner.
That sounds right. She was calmer last time when we kept it short.
I got paid. Want me to grab diapers and those sweet potatoes after the Sox game starts?
Yes please. Tiana said use the regular card and keep the receipt.
Got it. Also, I am putting Auntie K's $15 in the envelope with the other baby cash.
Thanks. I will mark diapers paid from your check and write the $15 on the folder note.
She made it halfway across the rug before I even got the bib on. Little speedster.
She beat me to the cabinet again when I grabbed the remote 😂
Keep the bowl on the counter until she settles. I only warmed the orange cup.
Was the latch still closed?
Good call. Last time I mixed in the green ones, she hollered like the Sox blew a lead.
Yep. I slid her back to the mat and she went right for the red and yellow pieces, pulled them apart, then kept pressing them together sideways.
I grabbed the last size-4 box and the little Red Sox onesie. Cart still looked empty without all Keisha's cousin requests.
Just offer two small bites first and then switch back if she fusses.
That is her favorite little project lately. I will leave the mat clear before bath.
Perfect. We only needed Hattie's stuff this run.
Yep. I'll wash the bottles when I get in, then we can put the game on low.
Did Hattie still chuckle at that little red puppet voice, or was she too sleepy after church practice?
She smiled hard, but I only let it run while I was folding right beside her.
That sounds about right. A few minutes with you there, then quiet music before nap.
After class snack went smoother when I gave her the little spoon and let her point. She reached past the crackers toward the banana pouch.
That sounds like her. Did she fuss when it was empty?
No fuss, just leaned forward and said something like 'mo nana' twice. Then she grinned when I opened the avocado cup.
I found the tiny jacket from the mountain visit in the diaper bag. Still smells like Grandma Denise's laundry soap.
Leave it in there. The station got chilly when we came back, even with it being a quick ride.
Okay. I am also putting $20 from my aide check in the castle envelope before I forget.
Good. By the time she is walking steady, we might actually have enough for that Orlando week.
The daycare lady called back. She said the home-history page looked clean, no extra numbers or documents needed.
Good. Tiana was worried she missed one of those back pages.
Nah, just asked who can pick Hattie up and who signs since our little boss still signs with applesauce.
Applesauce signature is very official.
We have infant music and blocks at the community center Tuesday at 9:30. Quiet room is open if the crowd gets too much.
That might work. I like anything where she can watch other kids and still come back to my lap.
Bring one family picture for the wall activity. We sing first, then stack cups and pass the soft books around.
I can stop by after work, but I'll tell Malik and Andre no running in the living room this time.
Good. She laughed at Andre's peekaboo last week, then crawled behind Tiana when he started hollering touchdown.
I'll bring the soft blocks and keep it short. If she starts reaching for bags and shoes first, we can let her check them out before everybody gets in her face.
That works. Tiana said she'll keep the bedroom lamp low and the piano list ready just in case.
Morning baby. I put Hattie's name on the prayer list and told Sister Carter she wears size 4 diapers now.
Thank you. We are down to the last sleeve, so that helps.
I can stop after choir practice with diapers and a little container of rice and gravy for y'all.
Come by after 6:30. Hattie usually calms when you sing low and rock her by the window.
Baby girl asleep yet? Those engines on Murchison were loud when I passed by.
Almost. Tiana closed the blinds after two men knocked about the roof work and Hattie jumped.
Call the office before opening up. I can come sit with y'all after my cafeteria shift.
Please do. The Bragg traffic is already thick, so take Grove Street if you can.
Tiana looked heavy after choir practice. I told her my porch is open if she needs a quiet place before taking Hattie home.
Thank you. The cousins keep sending the same phone video and the comments are making folks heated.
Let the grown folks breathe first. Denise can speak to them Sunday with love: stand tall, know what you can ask for, and do not get pulled into showing off online.
When I came in she was quiet until that sunny street intro popped up on your phone.
That one gets her every time lately.
I saw it. Hands patting, little squeal, then she crawled right to my shoe.
She kept reaching for the banana pouch after, so I gave her two more squeezes.
She was not having that blender noise. Tiana scooped her up before I even found the remote.
Is she okay now?
Better. Denise called and did that same Sunday tune over speaker, then Hattie quit rubbing her eyes and just stared at the lamp.
I kept my Red Sox noise muted this time. Learned my lesson 😂
I put the new dash cam in the cart. Same one Jamal said records front and back.
Get it if the check clears. I hate that we have to think like that just taking Hattie across town at night.
I know. Mama said her church group is doing that family safety workshop next Saturday too.
Put us down. I want her growing up with people who know what to say and when to stay quiet.
Hey love, the center printed comparison cards for the runoff. One column has paid family leave, child-care slots, and neighborhood response teams.
Can you hold one for us? Tiana wants to read it after Hattie's dinner, before the bedtime music.
I will. Pastor also mentioned the meeting about school lunches and the new traffic stops report.
Send the time when you get it. We are trying to keep up without dragging the baby through too much noise.
Good morning baby. I made extra grits and eggs if y'all want breakfast before church setup.
We will come by. The grocery run is waiting until Marcus gets paid, so that helps.
Bring Hattie's bag. I can keep her while Tiana handles laundry and those forms.
Thank you. We also put the new stroller tray back on the wish list for later.
Morning baby. I put Sister Elaine's squash casserole under your mama's recipe post, and I left a heart on Hattie's pink-bow picture.
Tiana saw it before breakfast. She said that casserole may be for grown folks, but the squash part gave her an idea.
Bless it. Tell her I sent the church ladies' prayer note by text too. For the shot schedule question, she should keep what Dr. Benson wrote and not chase every comment.
I will pass that along. She already saved the office printout on the fridge.
Good morning baby. I washed that church bag and folded the little leggings separate.
Thank you. We tried one pair and the waist was fine, but the sleeves on the tops are already short.
Bless her, she is stretching right out. I will bring the bigger shirts by after choir.
Good morning baby. I can come sit with her while you water those tomato buckets.
Anything soft is good. She keeps tugging at buttons, so plain is easiest.
Come on by. She has been reaching for the big green leaves all morning.
I’ll sing a little and keep her on the quilt. Then y’all can feed her before she gets too tired.
Baby girl ate good after her nap. I warmed the sweet potato and mashed it smooth with a little water.
Thank you. She does better when it is that soft.
Amen, she knew what she wanted. When I moved the banana bowl away, she pointed and said 'more' clear as day.
She has been doing that at breakfast too, especially with that bowl.
I can stop by after my shift. Also, don't let that video I sent stress you. I only sent it because folks keep asking.
I saved it but I'm not changing anything from a video. I messaged Dr. Rana's nurse to compare it with Hattie's chart.
That's the right move. Keep the clinic card dates and ask them about anything that sounds off.
Your cousin asked if Hattie has her own little page for birthday pictures.
No, just send her the two pictures from my phone if she asks. Please skip the cake-all-over-her-face one.
Okay. I will send the porch smile and the one with Denise holding her.
Perfect. Those are enough for everybody to see she had a good day.
Please do not start another clip unless I am back in the room.
I paused it. She kept bouncing when the potato face came on, so I knew she wanted more.
She can have a tiny bit after her bottle, but one of us needs to be sitting with her.
Okay, bottle first. I will wait.
Baby girl did so well after service. I kept her little clipboard from the nursery desk in my bag.
Was there anything left for Tiana to fill out?
Only the grown-up initials on the last two lines. The family-background questions were all no, thank the Lord.
I'll remind Tiana before bedtime.
I can bring the baby dress from last year's Juneteenth picnic if it still fits. It has the red ribbon, not too scratchy.
Bring it, please. We may just let her wear it for pictures after service if the room is not too loud.
I also have the little drum and the shaker. I will keep the cousins from banging them right beside her.
Thank you. She likes the beat when it is gentle, and Mama wants a few family pictures before everybody eats.
She did good during the clapping today. I saw you step out before she got too stirred up.
Yes ma'am, we sat by the side door just in case. Could I ask you something about the center's baby room when you have a minute?
Of course. Send it here or catch me by the nursery hallway. I can also check whether Ms. Renee still has those extra packs.
I will catch you by the hallway. I want to keep it simple.
Baby girl did sweet at church today. If you want, I can send that county office checklist I keep at the center.
Send it to Tiana, please. She said nothing is written into our budget unless there is an actual notice with Hattie's name.
That is wise. Keep every receipt and every card from family in one place until she decides what to open for Hattie.
For the center snack Tuesday, should I bring applesauce pouches or the soft diced fruit cups?
At the center, she kept choosing the basket with the ridged cups and little square snap pieces.
Applesauce, please. She has been grabbing the spoon herself, and the fruit cups turn into a whole scene.
That sounds like her. Did she stay on the blanket?

events.title: Denise here while Tiana runs errands
events.notes: Marcus leaves at 8:05. Keep Hattie's bottle, music, and nap blanket on the couch. Denise heads back before lunch.

events.title: Hattie 12-month visit
events.notes: Growth chart, regular shots, feeding texture questions. Ask about sleep stretch and ear tugging. Next routine slot penciled for June.

events.title: Community Center pool bag
events.notes: Pack swim diaper, towel, dry clothes, and the pink cup. Arrive early for the shallow-end group.

events.title: Hattie checkup - bring diaper bag
events.notes: Pack wipes, two bottles, vaccine card, soft snack pouch, and the blue blanket. Keep the 12:30 nap open after the visit.

events.title: After church: low lights, piano playlist, crib time
events.notes: Keep lunch soft and skip extra visitors before the nap.

events.title: Tub, jammies, rocking chair
events.notes: Warm wash, fresh diaper, lavender pajamas. Keep lights low; play the C major prelude track softly before the chair.

events.title: Living room game with Marcus and Hattie
events.notes: Put the little red B bib in the basket. Keep snacks low-mess and move Hattie back if the room gets too loud.

events.title: Pediatric portal forms - Hattie
events.notes: Bring insurance card, vaccine sheet, one car-seat label, and daycare packet with only Hattie's name filled in.

events.title: Hattie 12-month well check
events.location: Cape Fear Valley Pediatric Care, Fayetteville
events.notes: Bring blue record card, daycare form, and questions from the clinic handout. Ask nurse before using anything from the shared post Keisha sent.

events.title: Sort pictures from Panama City day
events.notes: Pick 6: boardwalk, striped blanket, stroller by rail, little feet after sand rinse.

events.title: Hattie check-in + shots questions
events.location: Cape Fear Valley Children's Clinic, Fayetteville, NC
events.notes: Bring blue folder, insurance card, snack cup, and list from Keisha. Ask nurse which date they want written on the daycare form since home notes only show the hospital week.

events.title: Library baby lapsit + card signup
events.notes: Bring board books to return, ID for account, and the small family photo book for the rhyme circle.

events.title: Print little album pages
events.notes: Use station stroller photo, Nana and Papa porch picture, and orange mouse-ear savings jar snapshot.

events.title: Little Tumbles mat room
events.notes: Pack socks, water cup, and the soft knee pants. Ask whether they are setting up the tape lanes again.

events.title: Drop March housing check
events.notes: Take stroller if the lot is calm. Use side entrance near Mrs. Green's building; avoid Bragg Blvd backup after 11.

events.title: Community center forum notes + baby bag
events.notes: Bring stroller fan, quiet toy, diaper pouch. Ask about pre-K waitlist, child-care vouchers, clinic hours, and body-camera policy handout.

events.title: Car seat check + parent resource table
events.location: Smith Recreation Center, 1520 Slater Ave, Fayetteville, NC
events.notes: Ask about child care voucher waitlist, WIC renewal papers, and the family safety table. Bring Hattie's folder and stroller fan.

events.title: Living room wind-down clips before dinner
events.notes: Queue short alphabet/counting video and red puppet clip. Keep banana cup nearby; pause if she starts racing toward the TV stand.

events.title: Prep Hattie's breakfast cups
events.notes: Mash sweet potato until silky; avocado from counter basket if soft enough; banana cup in fridge. Pause between spoonfuls and wait for her little 'more' sound before refilling spoon.

events.title: Morning service; ask Ms. Monique after benediction
events.notes: Bring bottle, soft blanket, and the clinic handout from Friday. Ask quietly about toddler swim times and whether anyone has extra size 4 diapers.

events.title: Service, nursery bag, covered dishes
events.location: Fellowship hall off Ramsey Street, Fayetteville
events.notes: Pack Hattie's ear covers, banana pouch, wipes, and spare dress. Denise bringing greens and cornbread. Monique asked about diaper sizes for the hallway table.

events.title: Sunday dinner at Denise's
events.notes: Pack Hattie's soft blanket, photo album from the top shelf, and the small speaker. Ask Aunt Keisha to keep the grown-up courthouse story short and end with the choir record.

events.title: Call Denise and Keisha after service
events.notes: Keep Hattie down for nap first. Let the aunties send links separately. Denise wants to say her piece about staying steady, carrying yourself right, and who to call if stopped.

events.title: McNeill family dinner
events.notes: Pack small blocks, banana pouch, blanket, and phone speaker. Use back bedroom after cake if doors start slamming or the big kids crowd her.

events.title: Stroller loop after snack
events.location: Cape Fear River Trail entrance, Fayetteville
events.notes: Bring soft blanket, water cup, and leave early enough for bath and crib before 7:15.

events.title: Hattie couch clip with Tiana
events.notes: One short clip only; sit beside her. Pause before supper if she gets wound up. She liked the red furry one last time.

events.title: Denise by after church supper
events.notes: Keep front room quiet after cousins leave. Tiana starts bath and bottle. Denise can take the rocker if Hattie is still red-faced; use the saved 'This Little Light' clip if needed.

events.title: Pick one 1st-birthday picture for family thread
events.notes: Use cake-smile photo only. Skip bath, diaper, upset-face, and house-number shots. Text to Denise and Keisha after bedtime.

events.title: Drop off Hattie's toddler gym forms
events.notes: Bring immunization copy, snack allergy note, emergency contacts. Adult-history section already checked no; Hattie's signature line handled by Tiana.

events.title: Living room mat before dinner
events.notes: Pull coffee-table basket up high. Put soft square pieces, textured cloth book, and ring stacker on the mat. Check cabinet latch by TV stand.

events.title: Check bin under crib before Walmart run
events.notes: Pull 12-18 month pajamas and socks first. Only buy missing basics if drawer still short.

events.title: Prep Hattie's dinner cups
events.notes: Blend two cups plain; set aside one with one new soft add-in. Serve before floor play so she is not grabbing the tray.

events.title: Call Denise before buying car seat base
events.notes: Check whether cousin's base is still in date. Hold Target cart for now. If it has to be new, split after Friday and next Thursday deposits.

events.title: March receipts and Hattie folder
events.notes: Add diaper, puree, and clinic parking receipts. Put Grandma's $20 with the birthday card. Do not enter any outside monthly amount on the fridge sheet unless a dated letter arrives.

events.title: Send Hattie photos to family thread
events.notes: Pick two porch pictures for Instagram story; reply to Aunt Keisha's sweet-potato question in texts; save Dr. Benson portal note for Tuesday morning.

events.title: Call peds nurse line
events.notes: Ask about two loose diapers after new sweet potatoes. Keep fluids, watch wet diapers, call back if fever or fewer wet diapers.

events.title: Community center infants: music, blocks, family wall
events.notes: Pack soft book, snack cup, wipes, and one printed picture with Grandma and Auntie Keisha.

events.title: Foam mats before lunch
events.notes: Bring grippy socks. Stay near the baby corner if the bigger walkers take over the slide.

events.title: Community center splash time with Monique
events.notes: Bring swim diaper, towel, backup onesie, snack pouch, and stroller fan. Leave before the crowded 10:30 group if she rubs her eyes.

events.title: Keisha visit before dinner
events.notes: Keisha bringing 18-month sleepers and can sit with Hattie while Tiana folds laundry. Marcus back by 5:40.

events.title: Extra mat play block
events.notes: Bring knee pants. Staff said Thursday group usually does the bell-start strip game near the end.

events.title: Pick up certified copy packet
events.location: Cumberland County Register of Deeds, 117 Dick St, Fayetteville, NC
events.notes: Ask clerk what proof is needed for Hattie's clinic and childcare folders. Take IDs, hospital bracelet photo, and the immunization card.

events.title: Lunch, walk, room dark
